title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student finished bandsaw training last week. Today she opens the makerspace assistant, and the program starts a new session with an empty message list and no saved notes. What does the model know about her training?

options.text: Nothing, because the new context window holds no record of it
Everything, because the model keeps what users told it earlier
Only the main points, since the model keeps short summaries
It depends on how large the model's context window happens to be

items.stem: In a simplified run, the fixed part (system prompt and tool descriptions) plus the question is 1,000 tokens. Two tool results come back, each of 500 tokens; ignore the model's own tool requests. The model is called three times: the first call sees only the fixed part and question, and each later call sees everything gathered so far. How many tokens does the third call send as input?
In one or two sentences: why does a long agent run cost much more than the total size of what its tools returned?
Your makerspace manuals total about 400 pages, and students ask many different questions. Which approach best keeps cost per request low while still answering from the right page?

options.text: Put all 400 pages in the system prompt, since the window is big enough
A search tool that returns a few relevant passages with page numbers
Save the 400 pages as a note that is loaded at session start
A one-paragraph summary of all manuals placed in the system prompt

items.stem: Which of these is the best candidate to save as a note that is loaded in later sessions?

options.text: The full text of the manual page found during today's search
The raw calendar entries returned by today's availability check
The date a student completed training on the laser cutter
The model's step-by-step reasoning from today's conversation
